aiManagement.title: AI management
aiManagement.description: Manage the shared daily AI question quota and AI retrieval and RAG service settings.
aiManagement.readOnly: This account can read system parameters. Changes require system:param:write permission.

quota.title: Daily AI question quota
quota.description: All users and application instances share one quota. It counts a question once when it starts at least one real LLM Provider HTTP request; quotas are not tracked per user or IP address.
quota.mockNotice: Mock mode shows the default daily quota of 50. Without a backend, usage and remaining counts are not shown and settings cannot be saved.
quota.reading: Loading the daily quota and usage statistics…
quota.readFailed: Could not load the daily AI question quota.
quota.invalidLimit: The daily limit must be an integer from 1 to 2,147,483,647.
quota.saved: The shared daily AI question limit was saved and recorded in the operation audit.
quota.saveFailed: Could not save the daily AI question limit.
quota.limitRange: Valid range: an integer from 1 to 2,147,483,647. The default is 50; set another value such as 99999 for an internal network if needed.
quota.noUsageStats: No backend usage statistics are available. Counts are not estimated or fabricated.
quota.sharedDescription: A question counts after it starts a model HTTP request, whether it succeeds, fails, or is cancelled. Questions that make no model request do not consume quota. New LLM calls are rejected at the limit.
quota.resetTime: Resets every day at 00:00 China Standard Time (Asia/Shanghai).
quota.footnote: The setting keeps the AI_LLM_DAILY_LIMIT parameter code in the existing system parameter table; usage remains in the shared business database. Updates require system:param:write and are recorded in the operation audit. Catalog COUNT, Mock questions, ordinary search, and RAG recommendations do not consume this quota.

rag.title: AI retrieval and RAG settings
rag.description: Configure local or external retrieval for AI questions and optional related asset recommendations on the search page. AI answers and citations are still checked against current DAP metadata.
rag.mockNotice: Mock mode shows defaults and the disabled state only. Persistent settings and service diagnostics require a backend connection.
rag.checkFailed: Could not check the RAG service.
rag.saved: AI retrieval and RAG settings were saved. Ordinary keyword search is unchanged.

statusDescription.disabled: The external RAG service is disabled. Ordinary keyword search and local AI retrieval are unaffected.
statusDescription.ready: DAP completed the external service health and readiness checks over HTTP. Returned assets are still verified against the current catalog.
statusDescription.unavailable: The external RAG HTTP service is unavailable ({{reason}}). Ordinary keyword search and local AI retrieval are unaffected; external mode does not fall back to local retrieval.

rag.retrievalModeDescription: Allowed values: local or external. Local uses the current DAP catalog and does not depend on an external service. External uses the configured, enabled service and does not fall back to local retrieval on failure. This setting controls AI retrieval, not ordinary keyword search.
rag.enabledDescription: Controls external service calls and provides the service for optional related asset recommendations on the search page.
rag.enabledValues: Allowed values: enabled or disabled. Configure a service URL before enabling external retrieval.
rag.strategyDescription: Current stored value. DAP's HTTP Search Service v1 request sends only query and topK, not this strategy field.
rag.strategyValuesDescription: Allowed values: auto, keyword, vector, hybrid. The RAG server's DAP_RAG_SEARCH_MODE setting selects the effective external retrieval strategy.
rag.topKDescription: Limits the number of candidates returned by the external retrieval service and processed by DAP.
rag.topKRange: Valid range: an integer from 1 to 20.
rag.timeoutDescription: The maximum time DAP waits for a response from the external RAG HTTP service.
rag.timeoutRange: Valid range: an integer from 250 to 10,000.
rag.serviceUrlPlaceholder: Use http://127.0.0.1:<port> on the same host; use https://<RAG_SERVICE_HOST> across hosts
rag.serviceUrlDescription: Enter an HTTP(S) service root URL without credentials or a path. HTTP is allowed only for localhost or a loopback IP; cross-host service URLs must use HTTPS. This URL is unused in local mode.
rag.tokenDescription: Set RAG_SEARCH_SERVICE_TOKEN through a deployment Secret. The token is not stored in the parameter table or sent to or returned by the browser.
rag.footnote: The management page or a manual check requests /healthz and /readyz; ordinary search does not run diagnostics. External service errors, a missing token, or catalog validation failures fail closed without affecting deterministic keyword search. DAP does not load the index or call the RAG CLI; the RAG server controls its retrieval algorithm.
